title: India gold market update: Gold demand gets festive boost
gist: World Gold Council's India update for October 2026: gold fell 6.3% to US$3,913/oz on Fed-hike expectations and a strong dollar, but Dhanteras/Diwali demand rose 15-25% in value and Indian gold ETFs logged a fifth straight month of inflows. Official imports remain well below seasonal norms as unofficial supply and recycling grow after the May import duty hike.

themes.theme: Gold price slide and INR effect

insights.claim: The gold price fell 6.3% in October 2026 to US$3,913/oz, a second consecutive monthly decline, driven by expectations of further Fed rate hikes, a stronger US dollar, an investor shift to bonds and futures selling.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Gold is trading against a hawkish Fed and strong dollar; a Fed pivot would be the reversal catalyst.

insights.claim: Indian domestic gold prices fell 5.3% in November 2026 to 12 November versus a 1% global decline, partly because the INR strengthened 1.7% since end-October; YTD gold is down 11% in USD but only 4% in INR.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Currency moves materially change local gold returns and thus Indian demand elasticity.

insights.claim: India's domestic gold discount narrowed from an average of US$66/oz in September 2026 to US$5/oz by 12 November as seasonal demand improved, but a residual discount to import parity points to adequate supply from old gold and unofficial inflows.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: The India premium/discount is a real-time gauge of local physical tightness.

insights.claim: Retailer estimates indicate Indian gold demand during Dhanteras and Diwali 2026 rose 15%-25% y/y in value while volumes were flat to slightly higher, despite festive-period prices nearly 10% above last year's.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Indian demand is proving price-resilient in value terms, supporting physical offtake on dips.
insights.quote: retailer estimates indicate that demand in value terms increased 15%-25% y/y, while volumes were largely flat to slightly higher

insights.claim: Indian jewellery buyers in the 2026 festive season bought more pieces but lighter ones, helped by promotions, new designs and lightweight jewellery, with old-gold exchange accounting for 40-60% of sales at many retailers.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: High recycling via old-gold exchange means retail sales overstate net new gold demand and imports.

insights.claim: Indian bar and coin demand during the 2026 festive period was concentrated in small 0.5g–5g denominations, reflecting token purchases.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Small-ticket buying suggests broad but shallow retail investment demand.
insights.locator: Bar and coin demand was also healthy

insights.claim: Indian gold ETFs recorded a fifth consecutive month of net inflows in October 2026 at INR35bn (US$364mn), 22% lower m/m but above the prior six-month average of INR24bn, with holdings up 2.2t to 126t.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Persistent Indian ETF inflows are a growing financial-gold bid independent of physical seasonality.

insights.claim: Indian gold ETF holdings grew by 31.3t in the first ten months of 2026, up 22% y/y, and 1-11 November inflows were an estimated INR24.5bn (US$262mn), adding 1.75t.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Momentum into November confirms Indian investors are buying gold dips via ETFs.

insights.claim: Indian gold ETF inflows held up even though domestic mutual funds temporarily suspended fresh subscriptions to gold fund-of-funds schemes in mid-October 2026, which World Gold Council reads as sustained interest in financial gold.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Supply-side frictions in fund products did not dent demand, signalling strong structural allocation to gold.
insights.locator: Continued inflows amid softer gold prices

insights.claim: Indian gold ETF investors added 64,163 folios in October 2026, taking total accounts to 12.74mn, showing a broadening investor base.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Rising account counts point to durable retail adoption of financial gold in India.
insights.locator: Continued inflows amid softer gold prices

insights.claim: Average daily gold futures volumes in India fell 30% m/m to 12.7t in October 2026, the lowest since January 2025, with daily turnover of INR176.5bn the lowest since August 2025, as falling prices reduced hedging and trading interest.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Falling derivatives activity in line with a global trend signals reduced speculative participation in gold.

themes.theme: Subdued imports and unofficial supply after duty hike

insights.claim: India's gold imports rebounded to an estimated ~70t (US$5.51bn) in October 2026, a six-month high and more than triple September in value, but 63% lower y/y in value versus 128t a year ago.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Official Indian imports remain far below normal, understating actual consumption.
insights.locator: Gold imports rebound, but remain subdued

insights.claim: India's combined September-October 2026 gold imports of ~93t were well below the 2021–25 average of ~180t, which World Gold Council attributes to unofficial imports and recycled gold, with unofficial supplies rising after the May import duty hike.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Higher Indian import duties are pushing supply into unofficial channels, distorting official trade data as a demand proxy.
insights.quote: Market feedback and persistent price discounts point to an increase in unofficial supplies following the hike in import duty in May.

insights.claim: India's official gold imports in January-October 2026 were US$47.36bn, down 6% y/y, with gross volumes of about 470t, down about 14% y/y.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Indian official import volumes are contracting meaningfully despite higher prices lifting values.

insights.claim: World Gold Council expects lower prices and the wedding season to support Indian jewellery demand, with investment demand steady, though a material price rise could temper buying.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Indian physical demand is price-sensitive: supportive on dips, a headwind on rallies.
